'''Mongla Port Authority''' is an autonomous organisation responsible for [[Mongla Port]] and is located in [[Mongla Upazila|Mongla]], [[Bangladesh]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Mongla C&F want SRO to unload imports|url=http://www.dhakatribune.com/business/2017/03/18/mongla-cf-want-sro-unload-imports/|work=Dhaka Tribune|accessdate=2 April 2017|date=18 March 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Enforcement of port state jurisdiction|url=http://www.thedailystar.net/law-our-rights/enforcement-port-state-jurisdiction-1281331|work=The Daily Star|accessdate=2 April 2017|language=en|date=6 September 2016}}</ref> The Chairman of Mongla Port Authority is [[Rear Admiral|Rear Admiral '''Mir Ershad Ali''']],  NPP, NDC,PSC .<ref>{{Cite web|title=Rear Admiral Musa takes charge of Mongla Port|url=https://www.newagebd.net/article/128467/rear-admiral-musa-takes-charge-of-mongla-port|access-date=2021-11-14|website=New Age {{!}} The Most Popular Outspoken English Daily in Bangladesh|language=en}}</ref>

==History==
The port authority was established on 1987.<ref>{{cite web|script-title=bn:ইতিহাস (History)|url=http://www.mpa.gov.bd/site/page/2fa934e2-3601-4fa5-b877-bd9bd4f04aa4/%E0%A6%87%E0%A6%A4%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%B9%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B8|website=mpa.gov.bd|publisher=Mongla Port Authority|accessdate=2 April 2017|language=en}}</ref> In 2013 Mongla port awarded the contract for 5 vessels from [[Timblo Drydocks Private Limited|Timblo Drydocks]] in [[Goa]], India.<ref>{{cite web|title=Timblo Drydocks secures five-vessel order from Mongla Port Authority of Bangladesh|url=https://www.porttechnology.org/news/timblo_drydocks_secures_five_vessel_order_from_mongla_port_authority_of_ban|website=porttechnology.org|date=15 August 2013|accessdate=2 April 2017|language=en}}</ref> Mongla Port Authority Chief Engineer Altaf Hussain was under investigation of [[Bangladesh Anti Corruption Commission]] for alleged grafts in awarding contracts.<ref>{{cite news|title=Massive corruption under probe at Mongla port|url=http://archive.dhakatribune.com/crime/2016/apr/18/massive-corruption-under-probe-mongla-port|work=Dhaka Tribune|accessdate=2 April 2017|language=en}}</ref> The same year the port authority signed a US$250 million deal with China for the modernisation of the Port.<ref>{{cite news |title=Bangladesh close to ink $6bn deal with China|url=http://www.dhakatribune.com/business/2016/08/25/bangladesh-close-ink-6bn-deal-china/|work=Dhaka Tribune|accessdate=2 April 2017|date=25 August 2016}}</ref> [[Dredging Corporation of India]] won a 1 billion rupee contract to dredge Mongla port from Mongla Port Authority in 2017.<ref>{{cite news |title=Indian firm bags Bangladesh dredging contract|url=http://en.prothom-alo.com/economy/news/137197/Indian-firm-bags-Bangladesh-dredging-contract|work=Prothom Alo|accessdate=2 April 2017}}</ref>

==Port management==
Mongla is the 2nd sea port of Bangladesh. The port is under the administrative control of the ministry of shipping, Govt. of the people's republic of Bangladesh. Chairman is the Chief Executive of the port authority. There is a board consisting of a chairman and three members i.e. Member (Finance), Member (Harbour & Marine), Member (Engineering & Development). The Board formulates the policy of operation, administration, finance & development of the port. there are 12 (Twelve) Departments to carry out day-to-day work of the authority. All activities of the port are controlled by the Ministry of shipping and monitoring by high powered parliamentary & Advisory Committees. The authority will recruit some personnel to speed their work in the port.<ref>{{cite web|title=Mongla Port Authority Job Circular|url=https://bdteletalk.com/mongla-port-mpajobsbd-com/|website=BD Teletalk|accessdate=17 December 2019}}</ref>
